items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Everybody I always liked, like Noon and Dodds and the old timers...

ctx.x: I rather the tone of an Alberts for different bands. Now playing with a combination of six-piece common Dixieland bands, I don't think a BAM clarinet fits in there. Because the tone is beautiful, rich and everything, but it haven't got the big tone when you get, especially when you get in the lower register.
Everybody I always liked, like Noon and Dodds and the old timers, they most of them have a big tone on that.
A big tone, you get a bigger tone out of, I think, out of an Alberts system kind of than you do a BAM.
